Inscribed by Zhu Yizi on the back of the container.　　Wang Zhizi was a native of the Eastern Han Dynasty during the reign of Emperor He, and died in the first year of the Yuanxing reign (105). His tomb is located 5 miles northwest of Mimou town in Xindu, Sichuan, in front of which a pair of stone queues are erected. The right queue is titled "Han Xian Ling Serving Imperial Shi He Nei County Order Wang Jun Zi Zi Que", and the left queue is titled "Han Yanzhou Assassination Shi Luo Yang Order Wang Jun Zi Zi Que". All of them are written in official script, and the characters are ancient, simple and robust, which have always been famous. According to Fangruo's "Essay on School Stele", "the full text must be obtained from the Song topography", but the Ming topography has been destroyed.　　In the Qing Dynasty, the right-hand side of the tablet was lost in the ditch and the text was completely lost. The left side of the tablet is also split from the upper right side to the lower left side, with only two words of "Han Dynasty" left intact, and seven words of "Yanzhou Governor of Danyang" lost from the small to the large part of the right side in turn, while five words of "Wang Jun Ziqui" do not exist. This is an old copy from the mid-Qing period.　　This is an old topography from the mid-Qing period, where the skewed strokes of the character "Yan" have not yet been danced, and the two dots of the "clip" part of the character "坂" are still distinct.
